classification.difficultyReason: Retain each standard inverse graph for non-negative inputs and reflect it in the y-axis, preserving its endpoints or horizontal asymptote.

content.prompt: Sketch these graphs using your knowledge of transformations.

answer.short: Reflect the right-hand half of $y=\sin^{-1}x$ in the $y$-axis. The graph joins $(-1,\frac{\pi}{2})$, $(0,0)$ and $(1,\frac{\pi}{2})$; domain $[-1,1]$, range $[0,\frac{\pi}{2}]$.
answer.worked: Keep the part of $y=\sin^{-1}x$ for $0\le x\le1$ and reflect it in the $y$-axis. The two branches meet at $(0,0)$ and end at $(\pm1,\frac{\pi}{2})$.

spec.description: Even inverse sine absolute-input graph with vertical endpoint guides and horizontal pi-over-two guide. Source answer blue is replaced by black.

answer.short: Reflect the right-hand half of $y=\cos^{-1}x$ in the $y$-axis. The graph joins $(-1,0)$, $(0,\frac{\pi}{2})$ and $(1,0)$; domain $[-1,1]$, range $[0,\frac{\pi}{2}]$.
answer.worked: Keep the part of $y=\cos^{-1}x$ for $0\le x\le1$ and reflect it in the $y$-axis. The two branches meet at $(0,\frac{\pi}{2})$ and end at $(\pm1,0)$.

spec.description: Even inverse cosine absolute-input graph with vertical endpoint guides and horizontal pi-over-two guide. Source answer blue is replaced by black.

answer.short: Reflect the right-hand half of $y=\tan^{-1}x$ in the $y$-axis. The graph has minimum $(0,0)$ and horizontal asymptote $y=\frac{\pi}{2}$ on both sides; domain $\mathbb R$, range $[0,\frac{\pi}{2})$.
answer.worked: Keep the part of $y=\tan^{-1}x$ for $x\ge0$ and reflect it in the $y$-axis. The branches meet at $(0,0)$ and approach $y=\frac{\pi}{2}$ from below as $x$ tends to either positive or negative infinity.

spec.description: Even inverse tangent absolute-input graph with outward continuation arrows and a dashed horizontal asymptote. Source answer blue is replaced by black.
